explanation:
Transcript: In the 1970s and 1980s, Lean was thought of as having originated in Japan. And a lot of global institutions visited Japan in those days and took away a series of tools and techniques that they thought were the things that drove change. These are things like quality management and just-in-time production. And the reality was they didn't get the value out of those tools and techniques that they thought they would, that the Japanese were getting. And over the past 10, 15 years, people have really started to focus on what are the principles that underlie those tools and how do you create a science around management. And really, this science has elevated the practice of lean to another level. And in recent years, in the past five or 10 years, people have even talked about what is the science of leadership effectiveness at the core of this.
